title: Meitowax (Long Island)
summary: Meitowax is a Long Island-wide name connected with map, patent, and historical variants including Matouwac, Metoac, Matowcas, Mattanwake, and Matowa.
introduction_content: Meitowax is one of the Indigenous names recorded for Long Island. The name belongs to a wider family of early spellings used in maps, patents, and historical accounts.
translation_content:
Meitowax is interpreted as the land of the periwinkle or country of the ear shell. Later scholarship preserves that interpretation while also questioning whether a Massachusetts-language comparison fully explains a Long Island name heard through New Netherland sources.

Why Place Names Matter

“Place names are geographical markers that can lead us on fascinating journeys into other cultures. They convey a people’s relationship to the land, their sense of place.”

— Allan Richardson and Brent Galloway, Nooksack Place Names: Geography, Culture, and Language (2011), publisher description
whereintheworld_content: Location note: The pin remains near the center of Long Island because the placename refers broadly to the island, not to one settlement, creek, or point.
